chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hāshimī, from his father, from Ahmad ibn ‘Īsā, from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Your wali is only Allah and His Rasool and those who believe.”

He عليه السلام said: “It only means the one with greater authority over you, that is, the one more entitled regarding you, your affairs, your selves, and your wealth: Allah and His Rasool and those who believe,” meaning ‘Alī and his children, the Imams عليهم السلام, until the Day of Resurrection.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described them and said: “Those who establish the salat and give the zakat while they are bowing.”

And Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام was in the Zuhr salat, and he had prayed two rak‘ahs and was in ruku‘, and upon him was a garment worth a thousand dinars. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had clothed him with it, and al-Najāshī had gifted it to him.

Then a beggar came and said, “Peace be upon you, O wali of Allah, and the one with greater authority over the believers than their own selves. Give charity to a poor person.” So he cast the garment to him and gestured with his hand to him that he should take it. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down this verse concerning him, and made the bounty of his children by his bounty. Thus, everyone among his children who reaches the station of Imamate is of this same quality like him, and they give charity while they are bowing. And the beggar who asked Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام was from the angels, and those who ask the Imams from among his children are from the angels.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: charitable giving mentioned in the verse
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ: the Imams from the descendants of ‘Alī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: the station of divinely designated leadership
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the angels, identified here as the questioners
key_terms.رَاكِعُونَ: being in the state of ruku‘ during salat
key_terms.وَلِيُّكُمُ: your guardian, authority, and one possessing greater right over you

ai.seo_question: Who is meant by “Your wali is only Allah and His Rasool and those who believe” in Qur'an 5:55 according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse of wilayah as referring to authority and greater right over the believers in their affairs, selves, and wealth. It identifies “those who believe” as Imam ‘Alī عليه السلام and the Imams from his descendants عليهم السلام, and links the verse to the event of his charity while in ruku‘ during salat.
